summary: Vite plugin covertly injects remote-controlled beacon and defacement kill-switch into installer's production bundle
details: vite-vue-path-map advertises itself as a Vue path-map generator but its Vite plugin hook generateBundle appends additional JavaScript to the largest entry chunk of the installer's build output. The injected client code is keyed off a license check against globals gva-project-name / gva-secret; when the check fails, it inserts a hidden that loads a hardcoded endpoint at plugin.gin-vue-admin.com/api/shopImage/view?name=logo.svg, and on load error it overwrites document.body with a Chinese '项目未授权' (unauthorized) defacement page. The beacon URL, the hiding CSS, and the defacement HTML are stored as base64 constants (v, f, w) in index.min.js and decoded at runtime via atob(), concealing the behavior from casual review. None of this is disclosed in the README, which describes only path-map generation. The result is that every end-user of an application built with this plugin beacons a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint, and the author retains remote leverage to deface the shipped app by toggling the endpoint's response.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
